newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand seeks to boost independence.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand seeks to boost independence.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Monday it was seeking legislative amendments to increase its independence and improve efficiency in supervising financial institutions.
Bank of Thailand (BOT) spokeswoman Duangmanee Vongpradhip told Reuters that the Bank of Thailand Act and the Commercial Banking Act needed to be amended.

"The move is to increase the central bank's independence. The idea received full support from the finance minister," she said referring to newly appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan.
Although the central bank is known to endear its independence, it is not free from political interference.
In the 1980s the BOT's governor Nukul Prachuabmoh was sacked by the then Finance Minister Sommai Huntrakul after differences between the two over how the nation's economic problems would be solved.

During the 1950s, another prominent central bank figure, Puey Ungpakorn, was sacked as a deputy governor after recommending a fine on a commercial bank despite a warning from military leaders not to do so.

The planned amendment of Commercial Banks Act would seek to strengthen the efficiency of the central bank's supervision of financial institutions, said Nongnart Sondhisuwan, deputy director of Financial Institutions Supervision and Development Department.
Nongnart said the amendment would seek to give the central bank more power in examining the performance of commercial bank executives and their internal controls.
"But I cannot give you more details. You have to wait until the governor reviews the draft proposal. He might say something about it later," she said. -- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
